Measured with scripts/report-free-space.py: landing-pad candidate area is the free copper patch south of the keep-out on the bottom layer (x 61.8-71.9, y 21.7-25.9, 42.4 mm2, pads must stay below y=24), feed corridors x 58.4-61.1/y 16.8-18.1 and x 58.8-60.5/y 23.8-25.9, about 19 mm per feed. Pad size/pitch and the matching network depend on the antenna form, which awaits the PN532 bench test.; inductance study (estimate-nfc-coil.py): the 17x21 mm reserve reaches 1.02 uH at 5 turns / 0.25 mm (C 135 pF, Q 127) up to 2.07 uH at 8 turns (C 67 pF, Q 173), so the bench test must answer read range and metal/ferrite loading rather than inductance; a card-sized 60x40 coil would give 2-3 uH with Q up to 219 but needs copper under the screen and MCU; layer choice: top-layer copper sits 3.0 mm from the front face and 1.5 mm from the back, bottom-layer copper is 0.7 mm from the back face, so the pre-study favours a bottom-layer coil unless the bench test needs front-side reading; feeder feasibility (pcb-maze-router.py, 2026-09-23): both nets route to candidate pads at (62.0,22.5)/(64.5,22.5) on the bottom layer - NFC1 18 segments + 1 via, NFC2 12 segments + 5 vias - but the paths split around the U1 module and form a large loop, so the maze result is a feasibility proof, not a recommended layout; the direct corridor (x 59.5-68, y 14-24) is blocked by roughly 40 top-layer and 37 bottom-layer segments from seven nets plus the C5-C7 VDD_3V3 decoupling row, so the antenna pass must also clear a 1.0-1.5 mm paired-feed corridor (re-route a few segments, optionally shift C5-C7 by 2-3 mm); then the two feeds can run side by side at 0.15 mm width / 0.3 mm pitch with no vias

evidence.charger_defaults: BQ25186 charge current is I2C-only (5-1000 mA, 10 mA steps above 40 mA): ICHG_CTRL (0x4) resets to 0x05 = CHG_DIS 0 plus ICHG 5+5 = 10 mA, CHARGECTRL0 (0x5) resets to 0x24 = ITERM 10% of ICHG, IPRECHG 2x ITERM, VINDPM 0b01, THERM_REG 100 C. Out of the box the sample therefore charges at 10 mA (about 0.2C for a 45 mAh cell, ~5 h); firmware should raise ICHGCODE to 15-20 (20-25 mA, about 0.5C) and leave ITERM at 10%.

evidence.assembly_channel: JLCPCB PCBA capability page scraped 2026-09-23: Economic PCBA takes single PCBs from 10 x 10 to 470 x 500 mm (panel 10 x 10 to 250 x 250), edge rails and fiducials are NOT required, 2/4/6 layers, 0.8-1.6 mm, single-sided placement, min package 0402, min IC pin spacing 0.40 mm, 2-50 pcs; Standard PCBA starts at 70 x 70 mm single / panel, requires rails and fiducials, goes down to 0.35 mm pitch but then needs a panel for our 84 x 52 mm board. Measured on the board (pad centres, not footprint names): U2 WSON-10 0.3988 mm is the smallest pitch, U4 SC-70-6 0.650, U5/U6 0.701 (the library footprint name says P0.35 but the part is a 3-pin 1 x 1 mm DRT SOT with three pads), J2 0.498, U1 module 0.798. The board is 2-layer (Gerber carries only GTL/GBL), 0.80 mm, all 56 designators on the top layer per the CPL, smallest passive 0603. Verdict: the card fits Economic PCBA as a single board with no panel, rails or fiducials; that channel only offers green + HASL at 0.8 mm and 2-30 pcs, and U2 sits exactly at the 0.40 mm floor, so Standard PCBA (panel >= 70 x 70 plus rails and fiducials) is the fallback if DFM rejects it.
evidence.usb_notch_datum: check-e16-board-clearance.py (new, 2026-09-23) intersects every real component solid from the exported STEP with the board material prism: the check FAILS because J1's model overlaps the board by ~11 mm3 in total (J1 body solid 4.64 mm3 x2 at x 76.00-77.50, envelope 0.76 mm3 x2, and a solid literally named 'Board' 5.68 mm3 x3 at x 76.72-77.49), all of it inside the 0.80 mm strip between the footprint's board-edge line and our drawn notch edge. Datums: the J1 footprint draws its board-edge/slot line at x = 76.704 (y 11.379-20.619) and the 12 'Board Outline to SMD Pad' DRC items are exactly the 12 signal pads (outer edge x = 76.504) sitting 0.20 mm from it; the GCT drawing's recommended layout reproduces our pad geometry through three dims (4.00 = shell-pad row spacing 77.104->81.105, 5.70 = outer shell row to the signal pads' inner edge 75.404, 4.60 = outer shell row to the PCB edge -> 76.504); a 0.70 mm shell-foot feature reaches x 76.00 (the drawing's Section A-A 0.70 dim). Our notch edge is drawn at 77.50, i.e. 0.80-1.00 mm east of both datums, so the board currently keeps a 0.80 x 9.24 x 0.8 mm strip that the connector body occupies. The counter-signal is the 'Board'-named marker solid whose east face is 77.487, but that solid overlaps the main board slab, so it reads as an assembly marker rather than a second board piece. Needs a physical check on J1 before the outline is changed; enclosure V7 would not need to change if the edge moves to 76.70.
